english: I go to work.
tip: Use åker for going by vehicle. Gå means to walk, so jag åker till jobbet means you ride or drive there.

english: We live on Vasagatan.
tip: Street names take på, not i: Vi bor på Vasagatan. The same på marks open surfaces.

english: He crosses the street.
tip: Över means across when there is motion: går över gatan is to cross the street.

english: She has eaten lunch.
tip: Strong verbs form the supine in -it: äta becomes ätit. Har ätit is the present perfect, has eaten.

english: She goes to the cinema.
tip: Gå på bio is fixed: cinema takes på, not till. Same pattern in gå på restaurang and gå på museum.

english: He lives by the sea.
tip: Vid means by or beside, right next to something: bor vid havet is to live by the sea.

english: We sit inside the gate.
tip: Innanför means inside a boundary, opposite of utanför (outside). Innanför grinden is inside the gate.

english: They are sitting in the car.
tip: Cars take i, not på: sitta i bilen. Swedish treats the car as an enclosed space you sit inside.

english: The cat is lying under the table.
tip: Swedish picks a body-position verb: things lying flat use ligger, so katten ligger under bordet, not är.

english: He does it for me.
tip: Åt marks doing something for or on behalf of someone: han gör det åt mig means he does it for me.

english: He lives on an island.
tip: Islands take på: bor på en ö. Swedish uses på, not i, for being on an island.

english: I have read that book.
tip: A definite noun with a demonstrative is marked twice: den boken (that book), both den and the ending -en.

english: We work at the same office.
tip: Samma never takes an article or ending: samma kontor, samma dag. It stays unchanged in every gender and number.

english: I have given him the money.
tip: Han becomes honom as an object: gett honom (gave him). Use honom after a verb or a preposition.

english: He has finished reading the book.
tip: Klart after a verb marks completion: läst klart means finished reading, like äta klart, to finish eating.

target: Jag vet att du har rätt.
english: I know that you are right.
tip: Ha rätt, literally have right, is the idiom for being correct: du har rätt means you are right.

target: Hon är lika lång som sin syster.
english: She is as tall as her sister.
tip: Equality uses lika plus adjective plus som: lika lång som means as tall as.

target: Vi vet inte om butiken är öppen.
english: We don't know if the store is open.
tip: Om means whether after verbs like veta: vi vet inte om means we don't know whether.

target: Hon började ett nytt jobb i Göteborg förra månaden.
english: She started a new job in Gothenburg last month.
tip: After ett, adjectives add -t: ny becomes nytt in ett nytt jobb. Neuter nouns trigger this ending.

target: Nya kläder kostar ofta mycket mer än man tror.
english: New clothes often cost much more than you think.
tip: Man is the generic you or one: mer än man tror means more than you would think. It is not the word for man.

target: Jag har arbetat här i snart femton år nu.
english: I have worked here for almost fifteen years now.
tip: For a span of time use i: i femton år means for fifteen years. Swedish uses i where English uses for.

target: Vi sparar pengar så att vi kan köpa hus.
english: We save money so that we can buy a house.
tip: Så att means so that, marking purpose: sparar pengar så att vi kan köpa hus, save so we can buy a house.

target: Varje sommar åker vi till stugan för att bada i sjön.
english: Every summer we go to the cottage to swim in the lake.
tip: Front something other than the subject and the verb still comes second: Varje sommar åker vi, verb before vi.

target: Jag har missat bussen tre gånger den här veckan på grund av trafiken.
english: I have missed the bus three times this week because of the traffic.
tip: På grund av is the fixed phrase for because of: på grund av trafiken means because of the traffic.

english: Stockholm is the biggest.
tip: Superlatives usually add -ast, but stor is irregular: störst (biggest). Stockholm är störst.

english: Sweden is bigger than Denmark.
tip: Comparisons use än for than: större än Danmark means bigger than Denmark. Än always follows the comparative.

target: Jag har alltid älskat svensk natur nu.
english: I have always loved Swedish nature.
tip: A time or frequency adverb goes between har and the supine: har alltid älskat, not har älskat alltid.

english: Drive slowly.
tip: The command form of köra drops the final -a: köra becomes kör, drive.

english: He is happier.
tip: Comparatives add -are to the adjective: glad becomes gladare, happier.

english: I have become sick.
tip: The perfect uses har plus a supine, and bli is irregular: har blivit.
